source_refs.note: Topic 23.7.2 (PDF 114); the aromatic examples are given in the esters figure of topic 23.7.1.

blocks.text: An ester is hydrolysed slowly to a carboxylic acid and an alcohol (or a phenol); the reaction is catalysed by acid or by base. Aliphatic esters were described in topic 23.4.1. Aromatic esters are hydrolysed in the same way, giving aryl carboxylic acids and alcohols or phenol: C6H5COOC2H5 + H2O -> C6H5COOH + C2H5OH (ethyl benzoate to benzoic acid and ethanol, H+ or OH-); C6H5COOCH3 + H2O -> C6H5COOH + CH3OH (methyl benzoate to benzoic acid and methanol).

blocks.alt: Two equations with H+ / OH- over the arrow. Ethyl benzoate (a benzene ring with C(=O)-O-C2H5) + H2O gives benzoic acid (ring with C(=O)-OH) + C2H5OH, ethanol. Methyl benzoate (ring with C(=O)-O-CH3) + H2O gives benzoic acid + CH3OH, methanol.
